chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a man accuses his wife [of adultery] and they perform li'an, then they are separated and she is not permissible to him forever; if he confesses against himself before the li'an, he is flogged with the hadd penalty and she remains his wife.

I asked him about the li'an in which the husband accuses her, denies his child, performs li'an, separates from her, and then says afterwards, 'The child is my son,' while contradicting himself. He said:

As for the wife, she is not returned to him forever. As for the child, I return him to him if he claims him, and I do not leave his child [disinherited]. The father has no inheritance from the child, and the child inherits the father. The child's inheritance goes to his maternal uncles. If the father does not claim him, then his maternal uncles inherit him, and they do not inherit from him. And if anyone claims him as the son of the fornicator, he is flogged with the hadd.

key_terms.جُلِدَ حَدًّا: He was flogged with the hadd penalty
key_terms.يَنْتَفِي مِنْ وَلَدِهِ: He denies paternity of his child

ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance and marital rulings for a child of li'an if the father later claims him?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the nuanced inheritance rules for a child of *li'an* (mutual swearing of adultery), establishing that while the child is returned to the father's lineage, the father does not inherit from the child, nor does the child inherit from the father. This unique bilateral disinheritance results in the child's estate passing to the maternal uncles (*akhwal*), a ruling that highlights the distinct Shia jurisprudential approach to lineage and inheritance in cases of *li'an*. The hadith further notes that if the father fails to claim the child, the maternal uncles inherit, but if anyone else claims the child as a 'son of fornication,' they are subject to flogging.
